subject: Egress origination policy, VPC wiring and approval path for private deploy
messages:
From: J. Martinez <jm@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: network-ops@acmehealth.com, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on egress/source IP behaviour for private deployment

Irene — thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we begin the network design review for our private deployment we need a concrete list of the outbound behaviours Redwood requires so our firewall/NAT/DNS folks can draft the safelist. Two specific asks from our side:  

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood requires static customer-facing egress IP(s) (i.e., fixed SNAT) for control-plane and model-serving flows, or whether you support a customer-scoped dynamic pool? If static is required, we need the IPs or CIDRs to add to our perimeter.

2) How does DNS resolution need to be handled? We run split-horizon DNS internally and do TLS inspection at the edge for some hosts — does that break anything? Do you rely on SNI for routing or IPs?  

Also attaching our standard safelist worksheet to speed things up. Please include any recommended port/protocols and a short justification for each entry so our audit team can accept it.

Thanks,
J. Martinez
Director, Network Architecture
Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_safelist_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: J. Martinez <jm@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on egress/source IP behaviour for private deployment

J — appreciate the clear asks. I pushed a compact requirements note back to your spreadsheet and put a PDF summary in the Drive link (see below). Key points up front:  

- Preferred model: customer-scoped static SNAT pool. For Dedicated/private deployments we can reserve a small customer-specific egress block for control-plane and telemetry so customers can allowlist a deterministic origin. By default we allocate a /28 from our managed egress pool for that purpose. Example (doc-only) range we use in examples: 198.51.100.16/28. This is documented and we commit to advance notice for any rotations.

- Optional mode: delegated dynamic pool if you prefer to route through your NAT/gateway with no Redwood-managed SNAT — in that case you must ensure stable outbound port reuse for long-lived streams and provide a documented handoff for traceability.

- Required outbound destinations/ports (minimum):
  * controlplane.redwood-inference.example:443 (HTTPS TLS 1.2+) — state and rollout control; MUST be reachable from the runtime control VMs.
  * telemetry.redwood-inference.example:443 — metrics/log ship (we support batching to reduce calls). Can be disabled for on-prem if you opt out of hosted telemetry and pass logs via your SIEM connectors.
  * models-cdn.redwood-inference.example:443 — occasional model/weights pulls during upgrades (can be pre-staged on an internal artifact mirror if you want zero external egress).
  * DNS (UDP/TCP 53) — resolver access required unless you host a local stub that resolves hostnames to provided internal IPs. If you run split-horizon, provide the internal zone we should resolve to and confirm whether DNS over TLS (853) is allowed; we can do DNS-over-HTTPS/DoT to an endpoint you host if preferred.

- TLS inspection & SNI: TLS inspection at the perimeter is supported, but if you terminate TLS and re-encrypt with a new cert (MITM proxy) please ensure SNI is preserved or provide a hostname-level allowlist instead of IP-only allowlisting. Some of our flows rely on hostname routing (SNI) to select customer-scoped backends in multi-tenant control-plane modes. If you must inspect, please provide a bypass for the following hostnames or enable an IP-based static SNAT so inspection doesn't break backend routing.

- Rotation and notice: If we provide a managed static pool we commit to >=14 days notice before any planned SNAT IP rotation. Emergency rotations will be announced to the security contact and via the support channel.

- Auditability: we can provide an egress evidence pack (signed list of sessions/flow logs for a date range) for SOC2/audit purposes. That requires a signed NDA amendment in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us whether you want Redwood-managed static SNAT (/28) or to NAT behind your gateway.
2) Provide the internal DNS entries you expect us to resolve if running split-horizon (or confirm you’ll allow our runtime to use your resolver with DoT).
3) Confirm whether TLS inspection will be applied to outbound 443 flows; if yes, provide a list of inspection boxes so we can validate SNI passthrough.

I pasted a short port justification column into your sheet and uploaded a one-page design note -> https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cEgR-Sample. Also attaching our internal design notes for your network team.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Lead Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-egress-design-notes.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, J. Martinez <jm@acmehealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on egress/source IP behaviour for private deployment

Irene — thanks for the thorough writeup and the drive doc. Quick approvals/constraints from my side before we lock into an approach:  

- Approve offering the customer-scoped static SNAT pool (managed by Redwood) for the controlplane+telemetry flows. Use a /28 by default; we can expand to /27 if the customer provides a business justification.

- Security constraints: require TLS 1.2+ and prefer mTLS for control-plane endpoints; if Acme cannot do mTLS we will require strict client cert pinning on their side or IP-based allowlisting.

- DNS policy: we will not accept TLS-inspecting appliances that drop SNI or rewrite hostnames. If Acme must perform inspection, they must provide a hostname-level mapping and ensure the cert-chain is preserved for outbound validation.

- Compliance: include egress flow logs in the evidence pack for the SOC2 review. Coordinate with sales/procurement to add the small amendment to the SOW for delivering logs.

Irene — please include a short paragraph for procurement/legal explaining the minimal SOW amendment needed and an estimate for how long the static pool allocation will take (we usually need 3 business days from signed amendment). J — copying your security and network aliases so they have context.

Thanks,
Laura
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: J. Martinez <jm@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: network-ops@acmehealth.com, security@acmehealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on egress/source IP behaviour for private deployment

Irene/Laura — this is very helpful, thank you. We will:  

1) Accept the managed static SNAT /28 for control-plane + telemetry (preferred for auditability). Please treat the example range as documentation only — we’ll await the final allocation and the 14-day rotation notice.

2) Our network team will host a DoT resolver for the project and provide the internal zone file for the split-horizon names (expected by EOD Thu).

3) We will not perform full TLS MITM for these flows; we can do SNI-aware inspection and will preserve hostname mappings.

Irene — please prepare the SOW amendment language and the flow-logs evidence template; I’ll route it through procurement. Also propose a 30-minute call Friday for a final priming session with our network and security engineers.

Thanks,
J. Martinez
Director, Network Architecture
Acme Health
